nodes.name: Frame
nodes.description: The frame is the structural body of the bicycle. On full-suspension bikes the rear triangle can move independently of the rest of the frame; components such as the rear shock, the headset assembly and the brake calipers attach to it.

evidence.quote:
The rear triangle of the frame,
which connects the rear wheel to the shock
absorber, can move independently of the 
rest of the frame on bikes that are fitted
with rear suspension.

edges.claim: The rear shock attaches to the frame at bushings — the manual calls them the frame attachments and expects wear there.

evidence.quote: The rear shock can develop wear at the bushing of the frame attachments.

edges.claim: The steerer tube bears against the frame: tightening the top cap draws it upwards relative to the frame and preloads the headset bearings. The manual states the relative motion, not a pressed-in fit, so this stays provisional.

evidence.quote: This draws the steerer tube upwards relative to the frame, putting preload on the headset bearings.
